messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm planning a KMS CMK rotation for the key used by service-x (secrets + S3 envelope) tomorrow 09:00 PT. I'll open a small TF change: enable rotation on the new key, create grants for the EKS IRSA role, and add a short re-encrypt job for SecretsManager. Can someone eyeball the plan when I post it?

priya: Which clusters and namespaces are affected? dev/staging/prod? Any downtime expected for pods that call decrypt?

alex: dev + staging first, canary to prod after smoke tests. No pod restarts required if we keep old key enabled until re-encryption completes. The tricky bit is ensuring the IRSA role has kms:Decrypt/KMS:GenerateDataKey on the new key before we switch secret versions.

matt: On the TF side watch out for cycles if you reference the iam role ARN in the key policy and the role's assume_role policy references the key alias. Share the plan output — I can look for "Error: dependency cycle" hints.

alex: Here's the change I'm planning to push in the infra module (trimmed):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "service_x" {
  description = "CMK for service-x secrets"
  enable_key_rotation = true
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
}

resource "aws_kms_alias" "service_x" {
  name          = "alias/service-x"
  target_key_id = aws_kms_key.service_x.key_id
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "svc_x_irsa" {
  name = "svc-x-irsa-${var.env}"
  # assume_role_with_web_identity config (IRSA) omitted
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "svc_x_irsa_grant" {
  name = "svc-x-irsa-grant-${var.env}"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.service_x.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.svc_x_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

sara: Quick note: aws_kms_grant only creates a grant that expires/exists outside the key policy — but some SDKs expect the key policy to permit the role too. We should also add a minimal key policy statement allowing the role to use the key, otherwise cross-account or tighter policies might block.

josh: Also remember that Terraform's aws_kms_grant can be tricky for rotation: grants are tied to the key material. If you create a new CMK and migrate, the old grants won't apply. If you're rotating in-place (enable_key_rotation = true) that's fine, but if you replace keys you'll need to recreate grants and re-encrypt secrets.

alex: Good call. Plan is to enable rotation on the same key_id (in-place) so existing grants remain. For the small window where we create a new key (if we end up replacing), I'll do this sequence: 1) create new key + alias -> 2) update role grants -> 3) run re-encrypt job to create new secret versions -> 4) point alias to new key -> 5) retire old key after 30 days.

priya: For re-encrypt, do you plan to use aws kms re-encrypt api via a short k8s job, or do we create new secret versions in-place? Need to ensure clients pulling secrets don't suddenly see incompatible versions.

alex: Plan is to create new secret versions (PutSecretValue with KMS key id) via a job that reads old secret, writes new version. That way SecretsManager still returns the latest version transparently. We'll throttle to avoid API rate limits.

matt: If you update the eks iamserviceaccount annotation to include the correct role ARN, make sure to run a `terraform plan` from the module root after pulling the role's ARN via data resource, not a computed value that causes unnecessary replacements. Example: use data.aws_iam_role.by_name to avoid create->read cycles.

alex: Thanks — I'll switch to data.aws_iam_role where possible.

infra-bot: terraform-plan: FAIL in infra/service-x on branch kms-rotate — error: "Grant creation failed: Invalid principal". See https://ci.internal/plan/1234 for full output.

alex: Pushed a small fix: added key policy statement to allow the role's ARN and replaced aws_kms_grant grantee_principal with the role's unique ID lookup. Re-running plan now.

josh: If plan succeeds ping me. For prod cutover, recommend a 2-hour maintenance window to run canary re-encrypt and smoke tests (decrypt call, Put/Get secret, S3 envelope ops). Document rollback steps: point alias back to old key and recreate old secret versions if needed.

priya: Also ensure CloudTrail logs for kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey are monitored during the roll so we can detect unexpected failures quickly.

alex: Will do. I expect a green plan in ~5m and will tag everyone. Thanks for the quick checks.

sara: One more nit — add lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } on the aws_kms_alias resource so alias swaps don't briefly point to null.

alex: Good call, adding that now.

matt: lgtm, thanks.
